Definition: from G1167; to be timid:--be afraid.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, on the night of the betrayal: let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid. The timid heart is the heart the Lord steadies with His peace.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the verse is the Lord's own answer to fear: His peace is the gift He leaves, and it is enough.
